core_obligations: From (3) to (1) (proof lines 11732-11740): a finite locally constant sheaf on a constructible locally closed subscheme is constructible, and a partition into finitely many such pieces makes the sheaf itself constructible.
From (1) to (2) (proof lines 11740-11746): constructibility is local, so condition (1) implies the existence of an open covering on whose members the sheaf is constructible.

From (2) to (3) (proof lines 11746-11756): given an open covering with constructible restrictions, the author uses the quasi-compactness of the constructible topology to extract a finite subcovering and then refines the partitions into a single finite partition by constructible locally closed subschemes on which the sheaf is finite locally constant.
proof_roadmap: Note that a finite partition into pieces on which the sheaf is finite locally constant makes it constructible.
Use locality of constructibility to get the local condition from the global one.
Use quasi-compactness of the constructible topology to turn the local condition into a finite partition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives three equivalent characterisations of constructibility on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme: constructibility itself, constructibility on the members of an open covering, and the existence of a partition into constructible locally closed subschemes on which the sheaf is finite locally constant (statement lines 11716-11730). The proof disposes of the implications (3) implies (1) and (1) implies (2) directly (proof lines 11732-11746) and then uses quasi-compactness of the constructible topology to extract a finite subcovering and refine the partitions, which gives (2) implies (3) (proof lines 11746-11756). The non-formal content is the refinement step, which is where the quasi-compact quasi-separated hypotheses are used. The claim is H2: two easy implications and one refinement argument.
